name: Crucible Industries Ceramic Stiletto CS-4 'Phantom Needle'
description:
A narrow-profile dagger constructed entirely from Ablonite-KR reactive ceramic, making it completely invisible to metal detectors and standard weapon-detection scanning systems. The Phantom Needle is 22 centimeters of translucent white ceramic, honed to a molecular edge that cuts with surgical precision. The weapon was designed for a single purpose: to pass through security screening and arrive at its destination undetected.

Ablonite-KR's reactive properties give the blade an unusual secondary effect — on contact with ferrous materials (including many cybernetic implant housings), the ceramic surface undergoes a micro-reaction that generates localized heat, effectively welding the blade to the metal it touches. Operators who understand this property use it to their advantage, driving the blade into a cybernetic joint and twisting to create a fusion bond that makes extraction agonizingly difficult without surgical intervention.

Crucible officially manufactures the CS-4 for 'ceramic materials testing and industrial sample preparation.' The weapon ships in a case designed to look like a laboratory instrument kit. No one involved in the transaction is confused about the product's actual purpose.
legality: Technically legal as industrial tool — functionally illegal as concealed weapon

blade_length: 22 cm
total_length: 32 cm
weight: 85 g
blade_material: Ablonite-KR reactive ceramic
detection_signature: Zero metallic, minimal density on X-ray
edge_type: Molecular hone — single-use sharpness

tactical_use: The Phantom Needle is an assassination tool designed to reach places where weapons cannot go. Its zero detection signature allows it to pass through security checkpoints that screen for metallic weapons, and its low density makes it difficult to identify on X-ray without specifically calibrated scanning. Operators conceal it in clothing, prosthetics, or purpose-built body cavities. The weapon's molecular edge is devastatingly sharp on first use but degrades with each cut — it is designed for one or two precise strikes, not extended combat.
cultural_context: The existence of undetectable ceramic weapons has created a persistent anxiety in GLMZ's security industry. Every checkpoint, every screening system, every pat-down carries the knowledge that Ablonite-KR blades can pass through invisibly. Security contractors have responded by adding chemical sniffers and density scanners to their screening protocols — measures that are expensive, imperfect, and have created a secondary market for ceramic weapons with masking coatings. The arms race between detection and evasion continues.
story_hooks: A Phantom Needle was found embedded in a Tier 5 executive's cybernetic spine — the reactive ceramic fused to the implant housing, and removing it would sever the spinal connection. The executive is alive but the blade is still inside.
Crucible's 'industrial testing' cover has been exposed by a journalist. The company's legal team is moving to suppress the story, but copies are already circulating in underground media.

physical_description.visual_profile: A needle-thin dagger with an almost ethereal presence — translucent white ceramic that catches light like frosted glass or ice. The profile is deliberately minimalist and non-threatening at casual glance, resembling a surgical instrument or laboratory tool rather than a weapon. The blade tapers to an impossibly fine point.
physical_description.dimensions: Blade length 22 cm, total length 32 cm (including handle), width at widest point approximately 1.2 cm, thickness 0.8 cm at spine
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light — only 85 grams — it feels almost insubstantial in hand, like holding a piece of advanced composite or crystalline material. The minimal weight distribution makes it ideal for concealment, with no noticeable drag or resistance when drawn.
physical_description.primary_material: Ablonite-KR reactive ceramic — a engineered ceramic composite with ferrous-reactive properties
physical_description.finish: Translucent white with a slightly frosted, laboratory-grade polish. The surface has a subtle internal luminescence in low light, appearing almost bioluminescent. No reflective shine — light passes through the material rather than bouncing off it.
physical_description.color_scheme: Translucent milky-white primary, with faint internal striations visible under direct light. Accent color is minimal — perhaps a barely-visible grip band in matte black or dark grey synthetic material.
physical_description.grip_texture: Minimal grip section, textured lightly for security without adding bulk — likely a thin wraparound of rubberized polymer or treated cloth that provides friction without visibility
distinctive_features: Molecular-edge blade that appears to vanish into a point — the edge is too fine to see clearly even under magnification
Translucent quality reveals subtle internal structure and micro-layering of the ceramic
Absence of any metallic components creates an almost ghostly appearance
Minimal guard or crosspiece — the transition from blade to handle is elegant and understated
No manufacturer markings visible on the blade surface itself — all identification is internal or on the handle
Slight internal cloudiness suggesting engineered reactive properties built into the material structure
The blade exhibits a faint opalescent sheen when tilted — light refracting through the ceramic rather than reflecting
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries designation 'CS-4' laser-etched into the grip section in microscopic text; 'Phantom Needle' printed on the grip in non-permanent coating that can be easily removed. Official industrial designation 'Ablonite-KR Sample Preparation Tool' appears on the included case, not the weapon itself.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically pristine on arrival — the weapon is designed for single-use or limited-use deployment and arrives fresh from manufacturing. After deployment, the molecular edge degrades visibly — the point becomes slightly rounded, and the blade may develop hairline fractures in the ceramic if used multiple times. Field operators often discard after 1-2 uses.
